description: The SECOND `keyword`-carrying control-flow site keeps the canonical identity too (issue #737). A `map` body is a value context, so an escape inside it raises `ol-return-in-comprehension` (`spec/execution-model.md:766-767`, `spec/error-model.md:116`) — and the Heritage spellings `output`/`op` report `params.keyword` `"return"` with `form` `"map"`, byte-identical to the diagnostic the Core spelling raises (`tests/conformance/core-language/check/return-in-comprehension` is the Core twin). This site is fixtured separately from the outside-proc one on purpose: the defect this closes was present at BOTH sites, and a fixture for only one of them would have left the other unprotected — which is exactly how the class survived two previous fixes. `params` is canonical; the `message` still names what the learner typed.
